verified_key_information_units.information: Cost optimization and energy transition efforts reduced electricity expenses through the new combined heat and power plant at Paljassaare wastewater treatment plant, which supplied 43.8% of site electricity needs and increased renewable energy consumption to 87% of total energy use (from 23% in 2020).

verified_key_information_units.information: Infrastructure modernization advanced with smart water meter rollout covering over 80% of customers (targeting 100% by end-2026), construction of 45.1 km of pipes (49% via trenchless methods), and launch of trenchless sewer rehabilitation service by subsidiary Watercom renewing approximately 6 km of pipes.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Investing for the Future; Watercom activities

verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Highlights from 2025; Sustainability Statement; Climate change section

details.completeness_justification: K1, K2, K3, and K6 are adequately covered with core material present in the candidate summary. K4 is partially present as it mentions smart meter deployment and the combined heat and power plant but omits details about pipe construction and trenchless sewer rehabilitation. K5, K7, and K8 are entirely missing, with no mention of drinking water quality compliance, environmental awards, climate targets, dividend policy details, or 2026 strategic priorities. The overall coverage is mixed, with most high-importance items partially or fully covered but significant gaps in strategic priorities and environmental performance details, resulting in a Neutral/Mixed assessment.
details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary is internally coherent. All statements are logically connected and support the overall narrative of positive financial performance. There are no self-contradictions, logical gaps, or organizational issues. The summary flows logically from revenue growth to cost management, profitability metrics, capital investments, and concluding remarks. While there are multiple numerical figures presented, none of the arithmetic relationships are presented as exhaustive additive components of the same total, so no contradictions arise from this. The progression from revenue drivers to cost management to profitability metrics forms a clear narrative arc without redundancy or confusion.
